planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall so eyes sit no more than 2 inches deep; hybrid peonies are slow to re-establish after disturbance.

directions: Red Charm is a herbaceous hybrid peony prized for its very large, fully double, deep red bomb-type flowers that open early in the season. Bred partly from Paeonia officinalis stock, it brings an intensity of color and an unusually rounded flower form to the garden. It performs best in full sun with rich, well-drained soil and benefits from peony rings, since its heavy flowers can bend stems. Divisions are slow to re-establish after transplanting but reward patience with long-lived, vigorous clumps.

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall so eyes sit no more than 2 inches deep; hybrid peonies resent being moved once established.

directions: Coral Charm opens in vivid coral-peach shades and gradually fades to cream as the large, semi-double flowers age, often showing several colors on the plant at once. It is an early-blooming herbaceous hybrid peony valued for its unusual warm coloring, a departure from the typical pink, red, and white of garden peonies. It grows best in full sun and well-drained soil and, like other hybrid peonies, resents being divided or moved once established. It has served as a parent to several other coral-toned peony cultivars.

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall so eyes sit no more than 2 inches deep; shallow planting is essential for reliable bloom.

directions: Louis Van Houtte is a nineteenth-century French heirloom bearing large, fully double, deep crimson-red flowers of rose form with good fragrance. It blooms in midseason and has a long history of cultivation in American heritage gardens. Full sun and well-drained, fertile soil keep the dark red color from bleaching and support strong stems. Fall planting of shallow-set divisions is recommended, as with other lactiflora cultivars.

planting.note: Plant in fall before hard frost, setting grafted plants deep enough to bury the graft union 4-6 inches to encourage own-root growth.

directions: Shimadaijin is a Japanese tree peony known for its large, fully double flowers in an unusually deep purple-red that can appear almost black-red in certain light. It blooms on woody stems in mid-spring and provides dramatic color contrast among typically pink and white tree peony cultivars. It grows best in full sun to light shade with rich, well-drained soil and benefits from a sheltered site that protects early growth from frost. As a woody shrub it should be pruned only to remove dead wood, not cut back annually like herbaceous peonies.

planting.note: Plant in fall before hard frost in a sheltered site that protects early spring growth from late freezes.

directions: High Noon is a lutea-hybrid tree peony bearing clear yellow, semi-double to single flowers marked with maroon flares at the base of each petal. It blooms in mid-spring on a woody shrub and is among the most widely grown yellow tree peonies for its reliable flowering and good garden vigor. It prefers full sun to light afternoon shade, well-drained soil, and a sheltered location to protect early growth from late frosts. It has long been a standard choice among yellow-flowered tree peonies in Western gardens.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall with eyes 1-2 inches below the soil surface; Itoh peonies establish faster than tree peonies but still take a few years to reach full bloom.

directions: Cora Louise is an Itoh (intersectional) peony with large, semi-double white flowers accented by light lavender-purple flares at the base of the petals, combining the flower form of tree peonies with the herbaceous, die-back-to-the-ground habit of garden peonies. It blooms in midseason with a light fragrance and strong stems that rarely need staking. Itoh peonies thrive in full sun to light shade with fertile, well-drained soil and, once established, require little maintenance beyond fall cutback. They are generally more disease-resistant and floriferous than many older herbaceous cultivars.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall with eyes 1-2 inches below the soil surface; Itoh peonies establish faster than tree peonies but still take a few years to reach full bloom.

directions: Garden Treasure is an Itoh peony bearing large, clear yellow, semi-double to double flowers with light red flares near the center, produced in great abundance on a vigorous, bushy plant. It blooms in midseason and is widely regarded as one of the most reliable yellow Itoh cultivars for garden display. It grows best in full sun with fertile, well-drained soil and, like other Itoh hybrids, combines strong stems and glossy foliage with a herbaceous habit that dies back in winter. Established plants can produce dozens of blooms per season.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall with eyes 1-2 inches below the soil surface; Itoh peonies establish faster than tree peonies but still take a few years to reach full bloom.

directions: First Arrival is an early-blooming Itoh peony with large, semi-double, lavender-pink flowers and a light fragrance, among the first intersectional hybrids to flower each season. It combines the bushy, sturdy habit typical of Itoh peonies with flower color reminiscent of its tree peony parentage. Full sun and well-drained, fertile soil give the best flowering, and the plant dies back to the ground each winter like a herbaceous peony. It is valued for extending the peony bloom season earlier than most lactiflora cultivars.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall with eyes 1-2 inches below the soil surface; Itoh peonies establish faster than tree peonies but still take a few years to reach full bloom.

directions: Callie's Memory is an Itoh peony with large, semi-double, soft yellow flowers edged in a fine rose-pink picotee along the petal margins. It blooms in midseason on sturdy, bushy stems that rarely require staking, a hallmark trait of Itoh hybrids. Full sun to light shade and fertile, well-drained soil support strong growth and abundant flowering. Like other intersectional peonies, it dies back to the ground in winter and is generally more resistant to foliage disease than older herbaceous cultivars.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall with eyes 1-2 inches below the soil surface; Itoh peonies establish faster than tree peonies but still take a few years to reach full bloom.

directions: Julia Rose is an Itoh peony noted for flowers that open deep coral-rose and gradually shift through peach to soft cream as they age, often showing multiple colors on the plant simultaneously. It blooms on a compact, bushy habit in midseason and has become popular for its unusual, color-changing display. It performs best in full sun with fertile, well-drained soil and, like other Itoh hybrids, dies back to the ground each winter while retaining the sturdy stems and clean foliage typical of the group. Established plants increase in flower count over several years.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall with eyes 1-2 inches below the soil surface; Itoh peonies establish faster than tree peonies but still take a few years to reach full bloom.

directions: Kopper Kettle is an Itoh peony with large, semi-double flowers in an unusual warm copper-orange tone that sets it apart from the typical pink, red, white, and yellow peony palette. It blooms in midseason on sturdy, bushy stems and combines tree-peony-like flower color with a herbaceous, die-back habit. Full sun and fertile, well-drained soil give the strongest color and bloom production. As with other Itoh hybrids, plants are slow to establish from fresh divisions but become vigorous and long-lived.
